body.p: After , and . On one EN 16931 UBL invoice, evaluating the Schematron that sxml compiles from the .sch sources costs 1.21 x 10^9 instructions; evaluating the official stylesheet compiled from the same rules by the ISO skeleton costs 0.55 x 10^9 (). The same rules, the same evaluator: the difference is in the stylesheet AST that src/schematron* builds (how patterns become modes, rules become templates and assertions become conditions, ), or in how the lowering treats it.

item.p: Mechanism: profile both runs (callgrind, inclusive, by template and by IR kind) and explain the difference before changing anything; then change what the Schematron front end builds (or, if the cause is in the shared lowering or evaluator, a general mechanism there that helps XSLT too), keeping 's semantics: first matching rule per pattern, every rule of a group, phases, let per rule context, locations of both kinds.
Owns: src/schematron*, tests/schematron_test.c, tests/bench/; the shared lowering or evaluator files only if the profile shows the cause there (say which in the D-record).

Done when: the explanation and before and after (instructions and seconds) in a D-record and the commit messages, on the invoice and on the 1,131 VEFA instances; Schematron findings byte-identical (JSON) on the 1,150 EN 16931 files compared; 7.30's suite 463 of 463 applicable; VEFA 1,133 of 1,133; if shared files change, QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole, base and change in the same setup: no outcome changes, case by case. Done 2026-10-28 (): the walk visited text nodes (@* | node()) and each visit calls every rule's match function; a pattern now walks only the node kinds its rule contexts may match. Invoice validation 1.208 to 0.479 x 10^9 (official 0.548), 0.362 to 0.296 s; VEFA 47.1 to 26.3 x 10^9, 7.5 to 4.7 s; findings byte-identical (1,150 files); suite 463/463, VEFA 1,133/1,133; no shared file changed.
